name: BeFunky
tagline: Photo editor, collage maker, and template-based graphic design

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 100+ digital effects; no account is required; the official page does not publish a numeric export cap.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Full paid editor, collage and design feature set; public pages do not expose a numeric AI-credit allowance.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $83.88. The current monthly checkout price was not exposed in the official public page.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 5,000 Batch AI credits/month plus the paid feature set.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $149.88. The current monthly checkout price was not exposed in the official public page.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 100+ digital effects; no numeric export cap is published.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; exact annual rates are public, while current monthly USD checkout amounts were not exposed
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pro's included Batch AI credits do not roll over. Purchased top-up credits remain recoverable for 90 days after downgrade or cancellation; mobile feature availability can differ from web.

verdictSummary: The visible photo + graphic design loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. BeFunky earns its keep through editor polish, assets, algorithms, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused local photo + graphic design editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whatYouLose: high-fidelity color, format, and export handling
whyPeopleStillPay: BeFunky: Creative users pay for speed, output fidelity, nondestructive editing, and years of edge-case work hidden behind direct manipulation.
ongoingBurden: Maintain file-format compatibility, GPU and canvas performance, undo history, export quality, and platform-specific rendering.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Open-source collaborative design and prototyping platform.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: A cleaner replacement for the template-and-collage half, with usable photo tools and exports on the free plan.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the Adobe Express desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly models power the generative features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, libraries and brand assets live in Adobe's cloud; exports include image, PDF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Adobe Express is shallower than BeFunky for dedicated photo retouching, artistic effects and fine collage control.

alternatives.name: Canva Free
alternatives.desc: Collages, social templates, and enough photo cleanup for ordinary humans; the serious retouching tools are elsewhere.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install Canva's desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Canva AI and Magic Studio provide generative tools; Canva does not publish a complete provider/model map for the free editor.
facts.dataFormat: Designs, uploads, folders and brand assets live in Canva's cloud; users export common image, PDF, presentation and video formats.
facts.gapVsPaid: Canva's photo tools are designed for quick layout work, not BeFunky's more focused retouching and effects workflow.

alternatives.name: Desygner Free
alternatives.desc: A free template editor with photo tools, collages, and brand basics; less glossy, but it keeps exporting.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.engines: Desygner's terms identify OpenAI-backed AI features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, fonts and brand assets live in Desygner's cloud; designs export as image or PDF files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Desygner's photo editing and collage controls are more basic and less polished than BeFunky's.

alternatives.name: VistaCreate Starter
alternatives.desc: Template graphics, collages, animation, and stock assets with unlimited downloads; advanced resizing still costs money.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads and the single Brand Kit live in VistaCreate's cloud; exports include image, GIF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: VistaCreate is a marketing-template editor first, with much less detailed retouching and collage control than BeFunky.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Penpot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Finished and maintained, but it designs interfaces, not collages, retouched portraits, or social templates.

rejectedAlternatives.name: PhotoPrism
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A very good photo library and a very bad collage editor; it organizes pictures instead of designing with them.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of BeFunky is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for BeFunky, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Canvas API.
Primary job: Build a focused local photo + graphic design editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: pixel-perfect professional tooling; large template and asset libraries; color-management edge cases.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
